docs.text:
Jaws!
I was 8 when I saw it. My parents regretted letting me watch it. We went on vacation to Florida & I refused to get on a boat or go in the water. Even home in Chicago, I refused to go in Lake Michigan til I was 11 when I accepted sharks are saltwater predators. That movie traumatized me!
If you are going to take an annual trip to think about folks who have died (and, weirdly, I recommend that you do), I suggest going onto and/or near a very large lake

I spent a whole summer as a lifeguard where my only job was to tell people they couldn't go in Lake Erie because of high bacteria levels. RFK Jr would have been one of the people we laughed at who we watched walk out of our sight lines to go swim in the poop water.
In 1982 I refused to swim in Lake Michigan because someone let an 8 year old watch Jaws. To this day my family hides sharks in my house. They have enlisted my wife. The most recent addition:
Heading home tomorrow having watched Jaws enough times this summer to be adequately prepared to swap Lake Michigan for the Atlantic Ocean for a little while.
I wasn't allowed to swim in the river growing up. Couldn't eat the walleye out of lake Erie. Parents were too paranoid. So, I say we can enjoy the comeback story, as a treat

Before you go back in a water this summer: My piece on how Jaws complicated our relationship with swimming 50 years ago. (And that includes fresh water Great Lakes and backyard swimming pools.) www.chicagotribune.com/2025/05/23/j...

50th anniversary of Jaws. I have a funny childhood memory of that film. I was 4 or so. We watched Jaws the night before we went to Lake Michigan. I had to get constant reassurance from everyone that there were no sharks in the water. I swam and had fun, but I did keep my head on a swivel in case
I saw Jaws for 50 cents. Those were the days. I was afraid to swim in Lake Michigan for three days afterward.
Lake Erie sharks, that bubble gum would never dissolve in my tummy, going blind from sitting too close to the TV.
I once swam in Lake Erie with some other kids in 1974. They started laughing and said "There's a dead fish in your hair!" I thought they were teasing me. But they were right.
I refused to swim in Lake Michigan after one of my cousins let me watch Jaws when I was 6.

Today’s 50 years ago the movie JAWS hit the theatre and ruined me for swimming in Lake Ontario for the summer. I was 12, my parents took me. But , it did peak my interest in SCUBA diving so that was good.

One of my coworkers went jet skiing on Lake Erie back in August, and she and everyone she went with got sick. She disclosed that her "ass had been like a waterfall for a week." It was funny, but also like, oh wow okay. She was kind enough to warn us when she blew up the bathroom.
#UTcommtheory

That same friend and I used to swim in Lake Erie not far from where the river spills into the lake. For years she liked to tell that story and say that she and I should probably be dead by now. Sadly she died of cancer a few years ago. She was 75.

I saw a pike eat a small dog on Lake Erie. When I was a kid, someone's pet lion got out and it was all over the news to stay indoors so you wouldn't get eaten by the lion. No less than 3 male teachers from my highschool were arrested/fired for making advances towards students and having CP.

He had so many! I was often given the side eye by adults in my neighbourhood for letting him jump in puddles and wade into the shallow waves of Lake Ontario on the little beach nearby.
We got a half-joking earful when he led the rest of his daycare class into the puddles, too. The boy’s had soakers.

I don't know what you have in mind, but I can think of a few things I dare not say in this forum. Let's just say there are some people who, if their bones were found in the trunk of a car at the bottom of Lake Erie, it would make me smile like that.

Thinking of when I was 4 or 5 and accidentally stepped in an ice fishing hole on Lake Ontario. As my grandpa pulled me up I worried about two things: losing my boot and having my leg eaten by a shark. Fortunately neither happened. 😊 www.usatoday.com/story/news/n...
friend of mine drown in lake ontario last summer. was a shock to all of us. good swimmer so we think maybe he'd drank a lot more than we knew, but. man. a few seconds in error is all it takes.
60 years ago we swam among dead fish in Lake Erie- my grandmother would go every morning to the neighborhood beach to bury all the dead fish that had washed up overnight
I never saw the ocean until I was 15 and this movie still messed me up. My older brother convinced me there were sharks in the Great Lakes and I was dumb enough to believe it.

Too young or perfect timing! I saw Jaws in an over sold theater! They legit set up folding chairs/let people sit on the floor! 70’s man! I didn’t swim in Lake Michigan for the entire summer. My best friends bro convinced us sharks could get in thru the St. Lawrence seaway and adapt to fresh water 😅!

One summer when I was a kid in vacation, I saw 2 kids drown in Lake Michigan from the undertow. One boy was floating on a blow up raft. Undertow pulled him right off into the water. He was near shore, but over his head.
4. JAWS. In the summer, I love going to the beach and then coming home and watching JAWS. (We swim in Lake Michigan. No danger of Great Whites.)

I was teaching swim lessons. I got felt up by a 6 year-old boy. Three times. The engineer, the deckhand on the great lakes or on the Mississippi or St Lawrence or Sacramento or Hudson or Delaware claims him.

My parents took us for our ocean(Chatham ,ma,)vacation from our town on lake ontario(not cold enough from Scotland where they grew up and Ontario was so polluted) in 1975. The drive in movie was,”Jaws.” Good times.
